name: Machnadebai
overview: Machnadebai is a male figure mentioned in the book of Ezra as a descendant of Bani. He is uniquely identified by his connection to a foreign wife, which highlights a specific genealogical detail noted in the post-exilic community. No further tribal affiliation or additional personal notes are recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Machnadebai is a proper name found in Ezra 10:40 and is possibly understood to mean 'possession of Nebo.' There is no indication that this name was given directly by God, and no titles are associated with it in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Machnadebai is explicitly recorded as a descendant of Bani, establishing a direct familial link. Beyond this, Scripture does not provide further family relationships or details concerning his lineage or descendants.
scriptureSignificance: Machnadebai's significance lies in his mention as part of the post-exilic community dealing with the issue of intermarriage with foreign wives, as recorded in Ezra 10:40. His identification as a descendant of Bani who had taken a foreign wife places him within the broader narrative of Israel's restoration and the call to covenant faithfulness. This brief mention underscores the challenges faced by the returning exiles in maintaining purity of worship and community identity according to the Law.
